physical_harm: Injuries caused by sharp-edged weapons leading to death
number_of_offences: Four offences/counts charged, three finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that deceased Harpal Singh suffered injuries caused by sharp-edged weapons, not bullet injuries, and that the charge framed was misleading as it attributed the death to bullet injuries sustained from a pistol.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) as credible in stating that Harpal Singh fell down due to the commotion caused by the firing of shots but were not aware whether bullets hit him or not. However, the court found that the prosecution's case was inconsistent with the evidence presented.

legal_representation.accused: Rakesh K Khanna, Sr. Adv., Ms. Shefali Jain, Samant Singh, Aditya Pushkal Khanna, Ramya Khanna, Ms. Archana Midha, Ali Mushtaq Newazish, Ms. Preeja Nair, Gurmeet Singh, Aditya Kumar Archiya, Rajesh Prasad Singh, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Vindo Diwakar, AAG, Sarvesh Singh Baghel, Pranav Kumar, B.N. Dubey, Vishal Kumar Singh, Advs.

investigation_status: Two separate FIRs were registered; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Omission to frame a proper charge under Section 213 and failure to put material circumstances in the statement under Section 313
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that accused no.2 Yaad Prakash fired four to five shots from his country-made pistol which hit deceased Harpal Singh, causing his death. They relied on the FIR and eyewitness accounts of PW-1 and PW-2 to support this claim.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the charge framed was misleading as it alleged that Harpal Singh died due to bullet injuries, whereas the evidence, including the post-mortem report, showed that he died due to injuries caused by sharp weapons. They also highlighted the failure to frame a proper charge and the omission to put material circumstances to the accused under Section 313 of CrPC.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principles that the framing of charges under Sections 213 and 313 of the CrPC must ensure that the accused is aware of the allegations against them to enable proper defense. The Court emphasized that failure to do so can cause serious prejudice and a failure of justice.
precedent_relied_upon: Jai Dev v. State of Punjab [1963] 3 SCR 489; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116 : [1985] 1 SCR 88
other_sentence_order: The Court set aside the convictions of accused nos.1, 2, and 4 and ordered their release unless they are required to be detained in connection with any other offence. Accused no.3 Diwan Singh was already acquitted.
